lastWeekReview.title: The Need for Judges
bullets: After Jericho, the children of Israel enjoyed peace — but then they turned their BACK on God and loved idols made of wood and stone.
This began the time of the JUDGES, when everyone “did that which was right in his own eyes.”
A judge is like an ARBITRATOR who helps everyone agree on a fair solution and keeps people following the law.
Judges are for our GOOD — they correct and discipline us so we behave the way we should.
God has set “judges” all around us — a mom settling a squabble, a serving one helping in the meeting, a principal at school.
We can ACCEPT God’s arrangement and receive help from the “judges” He gives us.
lastWeekReview.discussion: Did you have a moment this past week when a “judge” — a parent, teacher, or serving one — helped you do the right thing? Were you thankful they were in your life? Share how it went!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “Blessed is the man who fears Jehovah, / Who delights greatly in His commandments.” — Psalms 112:1

kidsContent.text: During the time of the judges, all the men of Israel failed Jehovah. So God did something remarkable — He raised up a WOMAN, Deborah, to sit as a judge over His people! While everyone else did what was right in their own eyes, Deborah did what was right in God’s eyes.

At that time, King Jabin was mistreating Israel. Why didn’t they fight back? No man was willing to LEAD, and no one was willing to FOLLOW a leader. Everyone just did their own thing — so they stayed stuck under Jabin. It was a miserable situation!

God needed BOTH: someone to take the lead, and some to follow. So Deborah called Barak, a capable military man, to lead 10,000 men. Barak was afraid because no one wanted to follow — “If you go with me, I’ll go,” he said. So Deborah rose up and went with him!

Sisera, Jabin’s captain, charged out with 900 iron chariots. Israel had none — but Jehovah fought for them! He threw Sisera and all his chariots into CONFUSION, and the whole enemy army was destroyed. Not even one was left!

🌟 God subdued Jabin, and Deborah and Barak led the people to sing praises to Jehovah. The land had rest for 40 years — all because Deborah followed God and led, and Barak was willing to follow a proper leader!

image.caption: Deborah the prophetess and Barak lead Israel to victory

kidsContent.text: When everyone does only what is right in their OWN eyes — nobody leading, nobody following — nothing good gets done. Just like Israel under Jabin, doing our own thing often leads to a miserable situation.

Even when you are young, you can be willing to FOLLOW the proper leaders God has set before you — your parents, your serving ones, and those who follow Him. To always do things the way YOU think is best is not the right way; it can lead to mistakes.

Barak followed Deborah, and everything changed — the men came into excellent order and God won a mighty victory. When we follow the leaders God sets before us, we stop doing whatever we think is best and follow God as our King again.
🌟 This week, let’s be like Barak — willing to follow the proper leaders God has placed over us, trusting that God is leading us through them!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, be willing to follow the proper leaders God has set before you! When a parent or serving one gives you direction, follow it cheerfully instead of insisting on your own way — just like Barak followed Deborah.

memoryVerse.text: The way of the fool is right in his own eyes, / But a wise man listens to counsel.
memoryVerse.application: Doing only what WE think is best — like a fool who is right in his own eyes — can lead us into trouble and a miserable situation. A wise person listens to counsel and follows the proper leaders God sets before us. Barak listened to Deborah, and God gave a mighty victory!

activity.title: ⚔️ Lead and Follow — Into the Battle

parts.text: Materials: A “Deborah” leader badge or sash, a soft “sword” or pool noodle for Barak, and open floor space marked with a “start” camp and a “river Kishon” finish line.
Setup: Choose one child to be Deborah (the God-appointed leader). Everyone else is part of the 10,000 men. Remind them: an army only wins when there is a leader AND followers who follow!

Round 1 — No One Leading: Tell the kids to cross to the “river” however they each want, all at once. It becomes chaos! Point out — this is Israel doing what was right in their own eyes, stuck under Jabin.
Round 2 — Deborah Calls Barak: Deborah taps one child to be Barak. Barak leads the line; everyone copies Barak’s exact path (march, duck, turn) toward the river, staying together in order.

Round 3 — Jehovah Wins the Battle: At the river, the leader shouts “Charge!” and the army rushes past the “900 chariots” (cones or chairs) knocked into confusion. The whole army crosses together — victory!
📖 Connection: When no one led and no one followed, Israel stayed stuck. When Barak led and the men followed, God won! We follow the proper leaders God sets before us.

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: Under a palm tree in the hill country of Israel. Deborah, the judge, sits and listens to the people. Barak stands nearby, and the people of Israel look tired and discouraged under King Jabin.
For years King Jabin mistreated Israel. No man was willing to lead, and no one was willing to follow. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes — so they stayed stuck. Then God raised up Deborah.
Barak, hear the word of Jehovah! Gather 10,000 men and go to Mount Tabor. God will draw out Sisera and his chariots, and give them into your hand.
Ten thousand men? Deborah… none of the men are willing to follow. They all want to do their own thing. I’m afraid to go alone.
God has spoken. Will you obey and lead?
If you will go with me, then I will go. But if you will not go with me, I will not go.
I will surely go with you. Rise up — this is the day Jehovah has given Sisera into your hand!
So Deborah rose and went with Barak, and 10,000 men followed. What a change! No longer everyone doing their own thing — now they were in excellent order behind a proper leader.
Ha! Israel has no chariots. Bring out all 900 of my iron chariots — we will crush them at the river Kishon!
But Jehovah fought for Israel! He threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into confusion before Barak.
Look — the mighty chariots are scattering! Jehovah has won the battle! Not one of the enemy is left!
This is what happens when we follow God and follow the proper leaders He sets before us. Come — let us sing praises to Jehovah!
The land had rest for forty years. All the children together:
We can be those who are willing to follow the proper leaders God sets before us!

description.text: Setup: Pick one child to be “Barak,” the leader. Everyone else is one of the 10,000 men lined up behind him.
Rules: Barak travels an obstacle path — around cones (the 900 chariots), over a “river,” under a rope. Every soldier must copy Barak’s exact moves in order, staying together.
Scoring: The army scores only if EVERYONE followed Barak’s path correctly — running ahead on your own idea breaks the line and loses the round.
Switch: Rotate a new “Barak” each round so everyone gets to lead and to follow.
📖 Connection: Barak led and the men followed, so God won the battle. We follow the proper leaders God sets before us!
Materials: Cones or floor markers, a rope, a “river” line, open space
Setup: Split into two groups — the “army of Israel” following one leader, and the “900 chariots” scattered as taggers across the space.

Rules: The army must cross from camp to the “river Kishon” together, following their leader’s exact route. When the leader shouts “Jehovah fights!”, the chariots must freeze in confusion for 5 seconds.
Out: Any soldier who breaks away from the leader and goes their own way sits out one turn, then rejoins the line.
Switch: Swap the army and chariots each round so everyone follows a leader and everyone gets to be a chariot.
📖 Connection: Israel had no chariots, but Jehovah threw the enemy into confusion when the army followed its leader. Following God’s leaders brings the victory!
Materials: Open space, a “river” finish line, pinnies or ribbons for two teams
Choose one leader to be “Deborah–Barak.” Everyone else is part of the 10,000 men and must stay in line behind the leader.
Goal: Only the leader chooses the path — over the log, around the tree, along the fence toward “Mount Tabor.” Followers may not shortcut or wander off to their own spot.
Rule: When the leader calls “Charge!”, the whole army rushes together to the finish; when the leader stops, everyone stops. Stay together as one army!
Finish: Gather at the top and sing a praise to Jehovah for the victory, just like Deborah and Barak did.
Materials: Just an open outdoor space with a few natural landmarks

outdoor.tip: ⚔️ The lesson is willing followership: Israel stayed stuck when no one would lead and no one would follow. Help the kids feel how good and orderly it is to follow the proper leaders God sets before them — instead of each running off on their own idea.
